output.title: Check the process before you automate it
output.body:
Before you build a regression suite around a workflow, ask a simpler question first: is the workflow stable enough to deserve automation at all?

For a small business owner, this usually means one repeatable task such as customer questions, invoices, or data work. If the manual version still changes from week to week, automation will not clean that up. It will just repeat the inconsistency faster. Efficient chaos is still chaos.

The practical test is not “can software do this?” but “can I describe this process clearly enough that someone else would follow the same steps and get the same result?” If the answer is no, the next move is not to automate first. It is to make the process visible.

Document one workflow on a single page: trigger, inputs, steps, edge cases, and the point where a human must still check the work. That gives you a real basis for deciding whether to keep it manual, standardise it first, or automate part of it later. Bareni’s diagnostic starts with that kind of workflow review: one recurring process, honest about where it breaks, and kept within human approval boundaries.
